highlights.title: NYT Cooking’s AI assistant saved my weeknight chicken, but almost ruined my cake
highlights.summary: Around 7PM each weeknight, I find myself standing in front of the fridge, trying to decide on something for dinner that won't make my husband complain, "Chicken again?" Yes, I should meal plan more, but I don't, so this is where I'm at. A nightly battle in which the chicken usually wins.
body: I tested the new AI-powered tool on ingredient swaps, recipe scaling, and a missing Bundt pan.

Recently, my best weapon in this fight has been AI. Between Alexa Plus in the Echo smart display on my kitchen counter, the Samsung Food app on my fridge, and even an AI-powered cooking robot, AI has become my go-to sous chef — albeit one I need to keep a close eye on. It’s helped me swap ingredients, generate ideas, fix things when I mess up, and yes, even cook better. So I was intrigued when my go-to recipe app, NYT Cooking, introduced an AI assistant.

Another great feature of the service, which I’ve been paying for for several years, is the reader comments. Here, I’ve often found solutions to cooking dilemmas, like what to substitute for makrut lime leaves — there’s always one slightly bougie ingredient in an NYT Cooking recipe that I don’t have on hand.

highlights.title: U2’s The Edge Wrote an ‘Elf’ Sequel, But It ‘Petered Out and Never Happened,’ Says Andy Richter
highlights.summary: According to Andy Richter, U2’s the Edge penned a script for a sequel to “Elf” — but fans will likely never get to see (or read) it. On a recent episode of “Obsessed: The Podcast,” the actor explained that Shauna Robertson, who’d produced the original film, once received a message saying that the…
body: According to Andy Richter, U2 ’s the Edge penned a script for a sequel to “ Elf ” — but fans will likely never get to see (or read) it.

“Somebody reached out to her and said, ‘The Edge from U2 has written a sequel to ‘Elf,’ and he wants to talk to you about it,’” Richter said. “It’s the weirdest story, but apparently it was fully written. Somewhere in the world there is an Edge-penned ‘Elf 2’ out there… I would love for that to make the light of day. It never happened. It’s one of those things where she’s like, ‘All right, sure, I’ll meet him,’ and then it just petered out and never happened.”

And yet despite how beloved the holiday classic remains 23 years later, Richter is steadfast in the belief that a sequel isn’t necessary at this point. “I’m on the side of ‘Let it stand,’” he said. ”Just let ‘Elf’ be ‘Elf.’ You don’t have to use every part of the animal.”

He continued: “Now that time has passed, the movie has become so special that I think that people, rightfully so, are loath to mess with it because we all can think of movies that have been tarnished by their sequels. And this is so special and so perfect and so beloved… Why risk it?”

highlights.title: The US let Nvidia sell chips to an empty office in China
highlights.summary: Concerns are being raised that neither the Commerce Department nor Nvidia are doing their due diligence when it comes to vetting Chinese firms cleared to handle the company's H200 AI chips.
body: The government is approving sales of Nvidia’s AI chips to Chinese firms with ties to blacklisted companies.

Only scant information can be found online about New Matrix, which was created 17 months ago. At the building that New Matrix lists as its address, a company directory does not include the firm. At the nearby property management agency for the industrial park, a receptionist and a manager both said they had no record of the company.

What little information can be found about New Matrix is concerning. Its owners have ties to a Chinese private equity firm that has been blacklisted by the US government since 2024. And according to the Times, this is not a rare lapse in oversight, but a troubling pattern of companies connected to entities with national-security-related trade restrictions being approved to purchase Nvidia chips.

highlights.title: 5 Incredible Anime Arcs That Are 10/10, No Notes
highlights.summary: Consider the Chimera Ant arc from Hunter x Hunter, which is nothing short of a rite of passage. It pushes the anime’s deconstruction of shonen conventions to its limits while sending Gon Freecss and Killua Zoldyck down starkly different paths.
body: An exceptional story arc can elevate even a flawed anime series. Although the mechanics of a great arc vary, the best tend to raise the stakes, test their characters, and build steadily toward a cathartic payoff. The conflict must also feel convincing, with the antagonist’s evolving goals and the heroes’ shifting motivations driving the story forward.

Perfection is subjective, but the finest anime arcs share a few qualities: They’re memorable, well-paced, emotionally compelling, and resolved in a meaningful way. With those standards in mind, these five story arcs come remarkably close to perfection. We wouldn’t change a thing.
What happens when a brilliant story ends with an equally brilliant final arc?

Fullmetal Alchemist: Brotherhood is filled with memorable stretches, from its exploration of the Ishvalan War to the heroes’ hunt for the Homunculi. But the anime saves its best for last with the Promised Day arc, a chaotic culmination of Father’s 400-year plan for Amestris and the intertwined destinies of Edward and Alphonse Elric.

highlights.title: The UV-tracking Gem made me rethink how sunlight affects my health, not just my appearance
highlights.summary: With temperatures rising to the 90s in Los Angeles, avoiding the heat wasn't exactly an option while I was at a relative's outdoor party in August. So I sat beneath a patio umbrella with a powerful fan nearby, figuring I was protected from the sun and heat.
body: What started as a test to understand how sun exposure was aging my skin took a turn that I wasn’t expecting.

Around the same time, I received a notification from an app used by the $249 ($149 at the time of publication) UV-tracking necklace I’d been wearing, called Gem, from a company called The90. It warned that my UV exposure had climbed considerably. It turns out UV radiation wasn’t repelled by this patio umbrella, and it’s hard to ever be fully protected because radiation can be reflected or scattered by objects in the environment. While UV exposure and overheating are different things, I’d mistakenly assumed the shade and the fan would adequately protect me from both.

This led to a discovery: One of my medications increases my sensitivity to heat, which helped to explain similar episodes I’d experienced over the years. The Gem didn’t diagnose anything, but it prompted me to investigate something I might otherwise have dismissed. Since then, I’ve been more mindful about limiting time outdoors during hours of peak heat and UV, staying hydrated, and paying closer attention to how I’m feeling outside.

highlights.title: Commander Shepard’s Actor Accidentally Immortalized One Mass Effect Race as Steve Buscemi
highlights.summary: Polygon spoke to Mass Effect's Mark Meer about how he joined the series and how he and fellow Shepard Jennifer Hale defined the character.
body: Mark Meer never planned on saving the universe, but the universe had other plans.

You know Meer from a lengthy association with BioWare’s most popular RPGs. He’s lent his voice to several of the studio’s games, from Neverwinter Nights to Jade Empire. Most famously, he voiced the male version of Mass Effect’s Commander Shepard, but his work with BioWare dates back to one of the studio’s earliest breakout hits.
“I did one line in Baldur's Gate 2, and then subsequently, BioWare just kept hiring me for every subsequent project leading up to the Mass Effect trilogy,” Meer said.

In the wake of EA shutting down BioWare, laying off its remaining staff, and canceling Mass Effect: Universe, Polygon spoke with Jennifer Hale and Meer, the voices of Mass Effect’s Commander Shepard. They talked about their hopes for the future of Mass Effect, but also looked backward. Both actors recorded for the studio’s Baldur’s Gate games. Meer would play “monsters and antagonists and that sort of thing.”

highlights.title: ‘Club Kid’ Scene-Stealer Kirby Howell-Baptiste on Playing a Drugged-Up Party Girl Who Turns Jordan Firstman’s World Upside Down: She’s ‘A Complete Tornado’
highlights.summary: “Should we do a bump?” It’s a line said, in various forms, numerous times across the first half of “Club Kid,” Jordan Firstman’s hedonistic and heartfelt coming-of-age comedy drama about a hard-partying New York club promoter suddenly forced to grapple with life and responsibilities.
body: “She’s a massive party girl — she never sleeps, she only parties,” says Brit actor Kirby Howell-Baptiste of how Edison was described to her. “She’s completely lost all social boundaries. The lifetime of drugs melted half of her brain away, and all her social cues and etiquette have gone.”
Howell-Baptiste’s etiquette-free Edison is only in “Club Kid” for a few minutes, but manages to steal the crucial scene in question from under the nose of writer, director and lead star Firstman.

Roughly quarter of the way into the film, she rocks up unannounced and chaotic, sporting green braids and oversized sunglasses, at the apartment lived in by Firstman’s nightclub promoter Peter (Firstman), with 10-year-old Arlo (Reggie Absolom) in tow. While wandering around the place like it’s her own, she reveals — in a hysterically matter-of-fact manner — that not only is Arlo his, but she’s brought the kid across from the U.K. to live with him permanently. Boom.

highlights.title: ‘I’m walking up hills!’ Maggie Beer on recovery, young fans and 20 years since the Cook and the Chef
highlights.summary: Ahead of her talk at the Powerhouse Parramatta Opening festival, the 81-year-old cookbook author and presenter says she still has a lot on her plate. Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email.
body: I t has been 20 years since the first episode of the Cook and the Chef aired in 2006, introducing Australian viewers to culinary odd couple Maggie Beer and Simon Bryant. Each episode the pair gently ribbed each other in Beer’s cottagecore kitchen in the Barossa Valley, then turned out dishes such as bruschetta, grilled kingfish and olive tapenade.
The show served up 154 episodes over four seasons – and who knows how many litres of verjuice. But there was a moment, in pre-production, when it seemed like the series wouldn’t get off the ground.

As Beer remembers it, their first trial in front of the camera was “hopeless”; they were riddled with nerves. But once the cameras were turned off, she and Bryant “sat on the steps afterwards and just talked and talked, and laughed and laughed, about how hopeless it had been”, and their executive producer could see their real-life chemistry. In the next few sessions on-set, their combined charisma and mutual love for cooking meant “we forgot the camera was there”, Beer says.

highlights.title: What does NAT type mean for online gaming?
highlights.summary: If you regularly play online games, you may have noticed a setting called NAT type or even got an alert about it. Here's what it means and why it matters.
body: NAT type isn’t always an issue, and depends on how your network is configured.

Inside an online game's settings or on your console you may have seen the NAT Type field and wondered what it meant. In some cases, you might even get a warning that your NAT type is strict and that matchmaking will be affected.

In many cases, this is more informational than anything you need to act on. If your game is working fine in matchmaking and voice chat, then adjustments shouldn't be necessary. But if your network is configured poorly for gaming and you keep getting disconnected or seeing errors, you should make some changes to avoid performance issues. Let's look over what NAT type means, how it affects you and what you can do to adjust it.

NAT stands for network address translation and is a key part of how the internet has worked for some time. IPv4, the original scheme for IP addresses, only has enough room for about four billion unique numbers. That was plenty when the standard was developed in the '80s but it quickly became stretched once everyone got online and started adding dozens of smart devices.

highlights.title: The No. 1 Horror Movie of 2026 Is Officially Leaving Peacock
highlights.summary: Not many directors can say their debut film was a blockbuster hit, let alone a cultural phenomenon. But newcomer Curry Barker, who wrote and directed Obsession, the No. 1 horror movie of 2026, can say he's accomplished both.
body: To date, Obsession remains the tenth most profitable film of 2026 at the worldwide box office according to data from Box Office Mojo, earning a gross total of $523 million during its theatrical run. It's no surprise that when Obsession moved to streaming, it continued finding success on Peacock, but going into November, the end of Obsession's victory lap is officially drawing near.

Obsession is leaving Peacock on Nov. 17, 2026, the same date that the film is expected to launch on Netflix in the United States. The film first hit Peacock on July 17, 2026, and drew in 456 million minutes streamed in just its first two days on the service, according to data from Nielsen. It went on to spend more than 150 days on JustWatch’s U.S. streaming Top 10 list, further cementing its domination in the industry.

Even Barker, who first built a following for himself making sketches and short films on YouTube, didn't expect the success that came with Obsession. In a June 2026 interview with the Associated Press, he said, "“That’s when you start to feel this impostor syndrome of like: What? It’s not that good. All I see when I watch ‘Obsession’ is the problems.”

The challenges extend well beyond French cinema. With fewer distributors acquiring independent films and arthouse theaters increasingly turning to mainstream Hollywood fare, even critically acclaimed movies are struggling to secure meaningful theatrical runs.

The definition of a French-language box office hit has also changed dramatically along with the health of the special market for most foreign-language films. highlights.title: The moment I knew: He said he was having a midlife crisis – I saw a man willing to face his fears
highlights.summary: Performer Jeremy Lloyd had a rule: no dating within the theatre and dance industry. He broke that rule with David. Find more stories from the moment I knew series. When David and I met, we’d both recently come out of long-term relationships and had our lives reorganised by the reality of mortality.
body: In early 2018 I was in my mid-20s, living in Sydney, and had just returned to dancing and performing after a three-year hiatus.
I joined the dating apps seeking affirmation that I could be desired again, and explicitly stated my HIV status on my profile.

Because my previous partners had been dance or theatre people, I had made a soft rule to not date within the industry. I broke that rule with David, although I didn’t realise it at the start of our first date.

That night, we drank two bottles of wine in his apartment and talked for hours. We covered everything from Netflix shows to movies we’d seen – intentionally avoiding talking about work. It wasn’t until I got up to go to the bathroom that I noticed the posters lining the wall. Productions he had worked on as a stage manager: Priscilla, Strictly Ballroom, West Side Story.

highlights.title: The disadvantages of owning smart refrigerators
highlights.summary: A smart refrigerator can change how you manage your kitchen, but its features come with practical drawbacks worth checking before making a purchase.
body: Before paying extra for a smart fridge, it helps to know what it could mean for your budget, your privacy, and software support over the years.

If you haven't shopped for appliances in a while, you may be surprised by how common smart models have become. To be clear, "dumb" ones do remain on sale. But even cheaper products frequently offer some smart home functionality, and the high-end models can include features like cameras and custom touchscreen controls. There are actually ovens with cameras despite what you'd assume from the heat involved.

The king of smart appliances, though, is the fridge. Once connected to Wi-Fi, many fridges will let you do things like check and adjust their temperature zones, or get alerts when maintenance is needed or the door is left open. The most advanced models — like Samsung's Bespoke Fridge with AI — can turn your fridge into a digital bulletin board, and even keep track of its contents.

highlights.title: Apps for Caregivers Get a Dose of AI, but That Might Not Be Enough
highlights.summary: The apps and platforms that help family caregivers manage their loved ones’ needs are becoming more capable, but the broader issue of caregivers’ well-being remains unsolved.
body: My husband and I are caregivers for our middle son, who has multiple disabilities and requires full-time support. We do our best to keep one another up to date on the activities that fill his daily life while also managing his numerous medical specialists, procedures, and therapies. We have to stay in constant communication while also working our jobs, caring for three teenagers, and managing a household. It’s tough.

We’re not alone in our struggles. According to AARP, in 2025, an estimated 63 million Americans cared for adults or children with a medical condition or disability. On average, these caregivers spend up to 27 hours per week providing care.

This caregiver crisis, where so many Americans provide ongoing, complex care and, as a result, endure poor health, financial strain, and isolation, is worsening as caregivers need more support and better systems.
Helpfully, to lighten the mental load, caregiver apps are aimed at families who are supporting seniors, children, or anyone with a diagnosis that needs regular management.

The Mercedes driver had led Norris by four tenths of a second after their first runs in Q3, but was then told to abort his second run when he was being held up by the Williams of Alex Albon.

Authorities saved the 17-year-old November 1, 2026, after receiving a tip relayed by a younger player she met while playing developer Innersloth's hit party mystery game…
body: The Utah teen was just 15 when she was reported missing in May 2025. Harmel allegedly began contacting her through Snapchat earlier that month before offering to send her money to travel to his home in Oregon. He then made the hours-long drive to her location and lured her into his vehicle, disposing of her phone by throwing it into a river shortly after.

Investigators said Harmel forced the teenager to sleep in a bed with him in his basement, becoming increasingly violent through the 521 days she was held captive. She found her window to escape when the alleged kidnapper granted her access to a phone without cellular data.

Although unable to contact others via traditional means, the device did allow her to use a WiFi connection to play online games. Among Us, which allows players to communicate and was released for mobile devices in 2018, allowed her to get in touch with another child.
After moving the conversation to a different, undisclosed social media app, she then told the other player who she was, revealing that she was actively being held captive at Harmel's home in Oregon.

highlights.title: How to predict the behavior of molecules from scant data
highlights.summary: A machine-learning approach called CheMeleon provides a practical way to develop new drugs or other molecules with much less detailed, expensive experimentation.
body: Discovering new molecules for specific uses is a major driver of progress in a wide variety of industries, whether it’s pharmaceutical companies looking for new drugs, or electronics or energy companies seeking new materials with particular properties. But it’s also largely a trial-and-error process, because there is not yet any way to perfectly predict how a given chemical compound will behave in terms of the myriad different properties and responses materials can exhibit.

Recent progress has been made on using artificial intelligence and machine learning to supplement or speed up laborious calculations based on physical principles that can at least provide some initial guidance on which compounds might be worth synthesizing and testing. Now, a new method developed at MIT shows that when there are few data on some technologically relevant property, such as ligand affinities for a recently discovered cellular target for a potential drug, this approach can outperform other existing methods for winnowing down the field of possible molecules that might be worth looking at.

highlights.title: Star Wars Zero Company studio Bit Reactor lays off staff, a month after bringing furloughed developers back
highlights.summary: Star Wars Zero Company developer Bit Reactor has laid off an unspecified number of staff, a month after bringing some of its furloughed team back to work.
body: Several developers announced on LinkedIn on Friday, 6th November, that they had been let go, as first reported by Bespin Bulletin. Bit Reactor hasn't said how many people are affected.

Among them is senior environment artist Ryan Lopez, who spent three and a half years working on Zero Company, from pre-production to launch, and was laid off after a three-month furlough. UI engineer Tyler Eichten, who worked on much of the on-screen UI for the game's tactical missions, and Ryan Mosher from the QA team have also confirmed they were let go.
"While it stings, I'm really proud of what we built together," Lopez wrote. "It was a privilege to ship a game with you."

Bit Reactor furloughed most of its staff in the weeks before Zero Company launched on 27th August, with one source putting the figure at roughly 80 percent. The studio appeared to have run out of money just short of release.
